identity.title: Rings and Gaps in Protoplanetary Disks: Planets or Snowlines?

paper_type_evidence.quote: We do not aim to provide a perfect fit to the observations, but use the structure to illustrate how the CO emission changes due to changes in the dust structure
We use the same data images as presented in (cite: Isella2016) for our comparison.

evidence.quote: The most recent parallax of HD 163296 is 9.85$\pm$0.11 mas using *Gaia* DR2, corresponding to a distance of 101.5$\pm1.2$ pc (cite: Gaia2018).
The most recent parallax of HD 163296 is 9.85$\pm$0.11 mas using *Gaia* DR2, corresponding to a distance of 101.5$\pm1.2$ pc (cite: Gaia2018).

question.value: Do gaps in CO emission in the HD 163296 disk imply gas density drops from planets, or can a snowline-like grain growth model explain the dust rings without planets?

evidence.quote: We use the physical-chemical code DALI to show that the gas temperature increases inside dust density gaps, implying that any gaps in the gas, if present, would have to be much deeper
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/ JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00601.S.
The most recent parallax of HD 163296 is 9.85$\pm$0.11 mas using *Gaia* DR2

what.value: Reduced ALMA continuum and CO isotopologue images of HD 163296

evidence.quote: We use the same data images as presented in (cite: Isella2016) for our comparison.
Stellar parameters are taken from (cite: Mendigutia2013).

what.value: Condensation temperatures: 23-28 K CO, 26-32 K CH4, 60-72 K CO2

evidence.quote: based on the condensation temperatures derived in Table 2 in (cite: Zhang2015): 23-28 K for CO, 26-32 K for CH$_4$ and 60-72 K for CO$_2$ respectively.

what.value: CO snowline at 75±6 AU from N2H+ and DCO+

evidence.quote: we overlay the snowline as derived from N$_2$H$^+$ and DCO$^+$ observations (cite: Qi2011) in HD 163296, located at 75$\pm$6 AU.

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: DALI models: Model 0 (no gaps), A (gap), B (snowline), C (deeper gaps)

evidence.quote: we have run Model 0 without any radial changes in the surface density or grain size distribution, and a variation of Model A with much deeper gaps (Model C).

what.value: Gap depths in dust and gas for Model A

evidence.quote: following the dust and gas model of (cite: Isella2016)
Further details on the parameters and assumptions in DALI are given in (cite: Bruderer2013).
Settling is parametrized following (cite: Bruderer2013)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA calibration and imaging details (taken from Isella et al. 2016)
DALI input files and full parameter set (gas-to-dust ratio, settling fraction, cosmic-ray rate)
Gap widths and depths for models with different delta_gas
Line-ratio/flux scaling used to compare model and data (model fluxes differ strongly from data)

analysis_steps.goal: Build parametrized HD 163296 disk with rings

method.value: Lynden-Bell & Pringle power-law with exponential cutoff surface density; gaps at Isella 2016 radii scaled to 101.5 pc

evidence.quote: we assume a surface density profile $\Sigma(r)$ as a radial power-law with exponential cut-off following (cite: LyndenPringle1974)

key_parameters.value: gamma = 1; gap factors for dust 0.010, 0.014, 0.17 and gas 0.4, 0.29, 0.56 (Model A)

evidence.quote: the dust surface density is decreased by a factor 0.010, 0.014 and 0.17 for gap $r_1$, $r_2$ and $r_3$ respectively
corresponding to a distance of 101.5$\pm1.2$ pc (cite: Gaia2018)

method.value: Model A varies surface density in gaps; Model B keeps density but sets large-grain fraction f_ls=0.01 in gaps, 0.99 elsewhere

evidence.quote: the fraction of large grains in the midplane $f_{ls}$ is set to 0.01 inside the three gaps, and otherwise $f_{ls}$=0.99

key_parameters.value: 190 radial x 60 vertical cells, time-dependent chemistry up to 1 Myr

evidence.quote: DALI was run using a grid with 190 cells in radial and 60 cells in vertical direction, using time-dependent chemistry up to 1 Myr.
We do not aim to provide a perfect fit to the observations, but use the structure to illustrate how the CO emission changes due to changes in the dust structure

validation.value: f_ls tested over a range; 0.01 or lower needed to reproduce ring contrast

evidence.quote: a value of 0.01 or lower is required to reproduce the dust continuum contrast seen in the rings of the observations

analysis_steps.goal: Compare model with data using enhanced image representation

method.value: Ratio of image to smoothed version (FWHM twice the beam), normalized; azimuthally averaged cuts

evidence.quote: for each image we compute the ratio between the original and a smoothed version (smoothing FWHM is twice the beam size of the observations) and normalize the result.

analysis_steps.goal: Explore gas gap depth and midplane snowline temperatures

method.value: Run models with delta_gas from 1 to 1e-2; compare Model B midplane temperature with condensation temperatures

evidence.quote: The values of $\delta_{\rm gas}$ range between 1 and 10$^{-2}$.

used_for.value: Physical-chemical modeling of gas temperature, CO abundance and emission

evidence.quote: We use the physical-chemical code DALI to show that the gas temperature increases inside dust density gaps
corresponding to a distance of 101.5$\pm1.2$ pc (cite: Gaia2018)

results_numeric.quantity: Minimum planet mass implied by gaps

evidence.quote: our models suggest that the gaps, if caused by planets, must contain planets which are at least a Jupiter mass.

findings_qualitative.value: Gas temperature and CO abundance rise inside dust gaps, so CO emission can brighten despite lower gas density

evidence.quote: Remarkably, even though the gas surface density has been *decreased* inside the dust gaps, the CO emission (in particular the C$^{18}$O) is *brighter*.

findings_qualitative.value: Snowline model reproduces dust rings with no change in CO emission

evidence.quote: The snow model can thus reproduce dust rings without changing the CO emission itself.

claims.hypothesis: Gas gaps in CO imply Saturn-mass planets
claims.experiment: DALI gap model with Isella 2016 depths compared with CO images
claims.result: Model predicts brighter CO in gaps, unlike the data
claims.finding: Gas gaps must be deeper, planets at least Jupiter mass

evidence.quote: The image data does not show an increase of emission inside the gaps, so the estimated density gap depths by (cite: Isella2016) are likely underestimated.

claims.hypothesis: Grain growth at snowlines can produce the rings without planets
claims.experiment: Model B with varied large-grain fraction
claims.result: Reproduces dust ring morphology without CO changes

evidence.quote: the snowline scenario is still a possibility.

limitations_admitted.value: Models not fitted precisely; inner region affected by continuum oversubtraction; combined hydro and chemistry not feasible

evidence.quote: We do not aim to provide a perfect fit to the observations

referee_caveats_inferred: Model fluxes differ substantially from observed fluxes
Model A and B compared qualitatively only
Snowline gap locations opposite to Model B assumption
Single object and only dust-ring structure from prior reduction

missing_for_reproduction: Reduced Isella et al. cubes (provided privately)

reproducibility.score_reason: Modeling-based, qualitative, DALI inputs and data reduction not given.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results are qualitative model comparisons, not derived from a stated reduction recipe.
